map.batch size 是不是越大越好？: Is a Larger Batch Size Always Better?
map.→ 打开批量大小迭代次数工具: -> Open the Batch Size Iteration Count tool
map.一万样本每批 32: Ten thousand samples with a batch size of 32
map.不是。大 batch 收敛快但泛化常变差，需配合更大学习率与更强正则；小 bat: No. A large batch converges fast but generalisation often worsens, so it needs a larger learning rate and stronger regularisation; a small batch has noisy gradients yet often generalises better, so you have to trade off memory against generalisation.
map.分布式有效批次=单卡 batch×梯度累积步数×GPU 数。: The effective distributed batch size = per-GPU batch × gradient accumulation steps × number of GPUs.
map.参数更新次数由\"样本数/批量\"决定而非轮数，直接决定训练时长与学习率调度横坐: The number of parameter updates is determined by sample count / batch size rather than by the number of epochs, and it directly determines the training duration and the horizontal axis of the learning-rate schedule. When the last batch is not full you must decide whether to drop it (drop_last): dropping keeps the BatchNorm statistics stable, while keeping it uses a little more data.
map.总优化步数=epochs×steps；batch 越大单轮步数越少但显存与通信开: Total optimisation steps = epochs × steps; a larger batch means fewer steps per epoch but higher memory and communication overhead.
map.最后一个不完整的 batch 怎么处理？: How Do You Handle the Last Incomplete Batch?
map.每轮步数 = ⌈样本数 / 批量⌉；总步数 = 每轮步数 × 轮数；最后一批大小: Steps per epoch = ⌈sample count / batch size⌉; total steps = steps per epoch × epochs; last batch size = sample count mod batch size (if the remainder is 0, use the batch size)
map.每轮迭代步数 steps=⌈N/batch_size⌉，N 为训练样本总数。: Steps per epoch = ⌈N/batch_size⌉, where N is the total number of training samples.
map.训练迭代次数计算器，输入数据集大小与 batch size 求训练 epoch: Training Iteration Count Calculator, which takes the dataset size and the batch size to compute the number of steps per training epoch, supporting deep learning training parameter setup.
map.默认保留尾批(大小不足 batch)；也可 drop_last 丢弃以避免形状不: By default the last partial batch (smaller than the batch size) is kept; you can also drop_last to discard it and avoid inconsistent shapes, in which case using a ceiling for the step count includes that tail batch.
map.：N=10000, batch=32 → steps=⌈10000/32⌉=31: : with N=10000 and batch=32 → steps=⌈10000/32⌉=313 per epoch; training for 10 epochs gives about 3130 steps in total. With 4-way data parallelism and per-GPU batch=32, the effective batch is 128 and steps drop to 79 per epoch.
